themes.theme_title: Clothing and Textiles — Advanced Garment Construction (Adults' Wear)
themes.theme_description: Construction of adult garments including women's and men's garments, traditional/cultural wear, alterations, neatening and modelling. Quality assurance and exhibition. Total periods in Term 1: 108.

topics.core_competency: The learner applies sewing skills and techniques to produce well-crafted adult clothing for a proper fit, durability, and style.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: a) construct adult garments to ensure durability and meet consumer needs
b) examine faults in constructed adult garments for quality assurance
c) display the constructed adult garments to ensure proper fitting and style

suggested_learning_activities.description: Learners use textbooks, samples of adult garments, magazines, newspapers, or internet tutorials to examine various sewing processes used in adult wear

Through think-pair-share, learners brainstorm: fabric selection and its appropriateness for different designs, styles and designs suitable for adult wear, colour choices and their impact on fashion, aesthetic designs choices and their visual appeal, understanding and incorporating customer preferences into design decisions
Individually, learners work outside the class to develop a garment design plan book with detailed plans for the articles they aim to create

The learner individually uses their previous drafted patterns, adapting them to selected sketched styles. They apply various sewing processes and aesthetic designs to create a range of adult garments — one of these garments should address a specific community clothing need. Garments include: a dress (formal, casual, party), traditional/cultural wear (Kanzu, Busuti, Gomesi, Mishanana, Kaftan), a pair of trousers, a shirt/blouse, a jacket

In pairs, learners critique each other's step-by-step workmanship during garment construction to appreciate the quality of work, identify faults, their causes, and possible corrections, and make a detailed write-up on the identified faults, their causes, and suggested corrections
Learners use existing literature and ICT (internet tutorials) to observe and rectify the faults in garments

In groups, learners use a flipped classroom approach to organise an exhibition to display their completed garments of various designs, demonstrating technical skills (visual merchandising, fabric knowledge, size, and fitting knowledge) and creativity

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Engage learners in a discussion to assess their understanding of the different sewing processes used on adult garments
Observe learners' ability to respect and engage with each other while presenting their findings

Evaluate learners' notebook and garment design plan books based on clear justification for the choice of designs, fabrics, and sewing processes, accurate and detailed sketches/illustrations, and logical flow and chronological order
Dialogue with learner as they construct various adult garments to evaluate their ability to engage in solving community clothing needs
Observe learners while they create a range of adult garments, focusing on their creativity and innovation, and evaluating how well they demonstrate the value of hard work and self-reliance
Critique the completed garments based on: Quality of construction, Fit and comfort, Design and aesthetics, Functionality, Care instructions
Engage learners in a discussion to evaluate their ability to examine garments, identify potential faults, explain their causes, and propose effective ways of mitigating or correcting these faults
Observe learners' level of cooperation and teamwork, focusing on their ability to work effectively in diverse teams

Critique learners' write-ups on faults and corrections in each other's workmanship based on clarity of description, categorisation of faults, use of supportive evidence, and impact on functionality and safety
Critique the garment based on: Tension of stitches, Neatness, Suitability of seams, Functionality
Observe learners' creativity and innovation skills as they explore possibilities in visual merchandising, fabric knowledge, size, and fitting knowledge during exhibition

Critique learners' displayed garments based on the use of a mannequin to check on the hang of the garment and the fit of the collars, correct positioning of style features, display fixture setup, safety considerations, and potential customer engagement strategies

syllabus_notes.text_verbatim: Sub-topics: 6.1 Adults' Wear: Women's Garments; Men's Garments (72 periods); 6.2 Alterations, Neatening and Modelling (36 periods). Total: 108 periods.

themes.theme_title: Clothing and Textiles — Soft Furnishings and Textile Industry History
themes.theme_description: Construction of soft furnishings and interior space decoration. Development of the textile, clothing and fashion industry including fashion history, cultural textiles, and mini-museum project. Total periods in Term 2: 108.

topics.core_competency: The learner applies basic sewing skills and techniques to create functional and visually appealing interior apparel for home décor and self-reliance.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: a) create soft furnishings that meet client needs
b) decorate interior spaces to enhance their appearance and feel

suggested_learning_activities.description: In pairs, learners use textbooks, samples of soft furnishings, magazines, newspapers, or online tutorials to examine types of soft furnishings in the interior spaces and their uses, brainstorm the guidelines for choice of fabrics, colour and texture, choice of aesthetic designs, and analyse the construction techniques and their procedures (e.g., appliqué, quilting, bead work, pile work, macramé, patchwork, needlepoint, binding, embroidery, piping and smocking etc.)
Learners make detailed write-ups of their findings

Using the soft furnishing construction techniques, the learner makes soft furnishings incorporating aesthetic design skills, and examines and critiques each other's constructed soft furnishings and decorative household articles (appreciate quality and identify the faults in the constructed fabrics) and make write-ups on faults and their possible corrections
Learners use soft furnishings they have constructed to decorate an interior space of their choice (sitting room, dining room, bedroom) considering the colour scheme and needs of the consumer

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Engage learners in discussions as they brainstorm, to assess their understanding of soft furnishings, particularly focusing on types and uses, choice of fabrics, colours, and aesthetic designs, and techniques used in their construction
Observe learners' ability to sort and analyse information as they explore the techniques and procedures used in the construction of soft furnishings
Critique the quality of learners' write-ups based on clarity of organisation and explanation of the notes, relevancy of examples provided, and use of illustrations where applicable
Converse with learners to assess their ability to create soft furnishings that can be used in decorating interior spaces
Observe learners as they make soft furnishings, ensuring authenticity and originality

Critique learners' constructed articles based on correct construction skills and application of aesthetic design, overall appearance, appropriate material choice and accessories, and functionality (comfortability, style)
Engage learners in discussions to evaluate their ability to enhance appearance of interior spaces, focusing on their colour scheme choice and how well they address the needs of the consumer

Observe learners as they decorate an interior space, assessing their creativity, innovation, and environmental awareness: use of innovative alternatives in design, waste management practices during the decorating process

Evaluate the completed interior space based on: Design intent and originality, Appropriateness and effectiveness of the colour scheme, Application of the elements and principles of design, Consideration of sustainability and ease of maintenance considerations

syllabus_notes.text_verbatim: Sub-topics: 7.1 Construction Techniques of Soft Furnishings (40 periods); 7.2 Designing Interior Spaces (12 periods)

topic_metadata.topic_title: TOPIC 8: Development of Textile, Clothing, and Fashion Industry

topics.core_competency: The learner explores the evolution of textiles and creates a mini-museum featuring traditional and contemporary textile pieces to foster heritage preservation, originality, and cultural diversity.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: a) analyse the fashion industry trends to develop innovative sustainable fashion solutions
b) examine the historical development of textiles across different civilizations
c) assemble various pre-existing, current fibres, and textile articles for a mini-museum exhibition

suggested_learning_activities.description: In groups, learners collaborate to compile a report on the history of textiles from a region of choice for submission to the school library. The report should include: research on textiles from the chosen region, relevant illustrations such as pictures, photographs, or drawings, integration of ICT tools to enhance their report, proper referencing sources, a cover page containing the report's title, the class, the date of submission, and the details of group members

Use of magazines, photographs, printouts from the internet and library to brainstorm reasons for wearing clothes, why the variations in clothing worldwide, and factors that influence fashion trends, and explore fashion, fads, style and fashion cycles (include how the cultural wears evolved e.g., Gomesi, Kanzu, Busuuti, Suuka, Mishanana) over time. Learners will also suggest possible alterations to current fashion trends
Using fashion magazines, images from the internet, newspapers, learners collect and compile different fashion samples and make fashion albums. Learners critique each other's fashion albums

Learners draw on their personal experiences with folktales, cultural activities, literature, and traditional attire to share ideas and insights about the history and development of textiles in their cultures

In groups, learners select a civilization and investigate the origin of different textiles across cultures. For example: Silk production in China, Cotton weaving in Egypt, Wool processing in Europe, Backcloth production in Uganda. Each group prepares a detailed case study covering traditional techniques, textile origin, materials used, and how traditional elements have influenced contemporary textile designs

In groups, develop a comprehensive questionnaire that includes: Name of textile, Type of textile, Country of origin, Ideal use, Unique characteristics, Evolution of the textiles over time. Purpose: The questionnaire will guide study visits to fabric shops, markets, cultural sites, museums, textile factories, and garment construction workshops. Where possible, learners should use smartphones to take pictures and video recordings

Individually, learners collect textile samples and create a fabric swatch that documents their findings detailing the evolution from traditional to contemporary fibres, fabrics, and textile articles. In class, learners display their fabric swatches for a gallery walk

In groups, learners collaborate to create a mini-museum featuring a curated collection of items including various fibres, textile articles, fabric swatches, videos, and images. The exhibits should highlight a range of textile elements from historical to contemporary contexts, with examples from Uganda and international sources. A gallery walk follows. Deadline: The completed project must be submitted by end of Term Two

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Engage in dialogue with learners as they brainstorm and present their findings to evaluate their understanding of trends in the fashion industry over time
Observe learners' critical thinking ability as they compare various perspectives on the reasons for wearing clothes and the factors that contribute to clothing variations worldwide
Critique learners' write-ups, focusing on the accuracy, relevancy, and depth of the information provided
Discuss with learners as they collect sample items for the fashion albums to establish their understanding of fashion styles and cycles

Critique learners' fashion albums based on sequential arrangement of fashion trends, name and year of fashion trend, type of fashion trend, compilation and description/illustration of different fashion samples, and neatness of the fashion album
Engage in discussions with learners to evaluate their ability to critically assess the historical development of traditional textiles: types of textiles, origin of textiles, evolution and usage
Monitor and assess learners' engagement and demonstration of diversity and multicultural skills as they share insights about their respective cultures
Engage learners in discussions to evaluate their understanding of textile origins, materials used, and traditional techniques
Monitor learners' collaboration, self-directed learning, and time management skills
Engage in conversations with learners as they develop the questionnaire, focusing on the clarity and relevance of their guiding questions for the field study
Observe learners as they sort and analyse information within the fabric swatch books
Review and critique learners' fabric swatch books and questionnaire: visual and artefact collection, content accuracy and relevance

Engage in conversations with learners as they create a mini-museum, checking their understanding of each item's historical background, cultural significance, and contribution to Uganda's textile heritage
Observe learners during the mini-museum setup to evaluate their participation, teamwork, and creative skills
Assess the assembled mini-museum based on exhibit setup, historical accuracy, and diversity and description

project_requirements.project_scope_verbatim: In groups, learners collaborate to create a mini-museum featuring a curated collection of items, including various fibres, textile articles, fabric swatches, videos, and images. Content focus: The exhibits should highlight a range of textile elements historical to contemporary contexts, with examples from Uganda and international sources.
project_requirements.deliverables_verbatim: The completed project must be submitted by end of Term Two. A gallery walk follows the mini-museum setup, where each group leads a gallery walk and all participants provide constructive feedback on each other's display.

suggested_uses: Integration of ICT tools to enhance research reports
Smartphones for pictures and video recordings during field visits

syllabus_notes.text_verbatim: Sub-topics: 8.1 Fashion Industry Trends and Fashion Cycles (18 periods); 8.2 History of Textiles and Clothing Worldwide and in Uganda (18 periods); 8.3 Evolution of Textiles from Different Cultures (20 periods). Project: The completed mini-museum project must be submitted by end of Term Two.

themes.theme_title: Clothing and Textiles — Marketing Quality Textile Products
themes.theme_description: Quality control standards, product costing and pricing, and marketing strategies for textile products. Total periods in Term 3: 72.

topics.core_competency: The learner creates and applies marketing strategies that showcase textile quality, meet customer needs and promote sustainability.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: a) evaluate the quality control standards for textile products to ensure customer satisfaction and enhance brand reputation
b) cost products for profitability and consumer satisfaction
c) sell high quality textile and clothing products to maximize market turnover

suggested_learning_activities.description: Through role play, learners work in teams: one group acts as quality control inspectors, while the other group acts as manufacturers. Using mock textile samples, the quality control inspectors evaluate each product against a set of acceptable standards (fabric strength, seam layout, stitching quality, edge finishing, and garment fitting) and provide constructive feedback. Following the role-play, each team produces a written report detailing their feedback, clearly outlining strengths and areas for improvement

In pairs, learners use textbooks and ICT to examine the essential elements of costing and pricing, such as: direct production costs (raw materials, labour and wastage), overhead costs (fixed overheads e.g., rent, machine depreciation, and indirect overheads e.g., wages, equipment operating costs), other operating costs (packaging, branding, and labeling) to determine the selling price
Learners make detailed write-ups of their findings and present them
In groups, learners generate a costing and pricing checklists on manila/flip-charts and display them in the classroom for a gallery walk
Learners cost and price any textile and clothing product of their choice and share in a plenary session

In groups, learners use the library or ICT to analyse the components of product marketing and selling: Product marketing, Product positioning and messaging, Advertising and promotions using ICT (social media campaigns or influencing partnerships), Customer handling and follow-up (customer retention, record keeping), Selling of the product to increase product visibility and turnover
Learners exhibit and sell their textile and clothing products

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Engage learners in discussions to evaluate their understanding of quality standards for textile products, including key attributes such as textile strength, stitching techniques, and finishing details

Observe learners' collaboration within their teams, assessing their ability to work effectively in assigned roles, provide constructive guidance on improving textile quality, and adhere to established quality standards
Review the inspectors' final reports based on: Fabric strength, Stitching techniques, Logical questioning by inspectors to manufacturers, Appropriate response from manufacturers
Engage in discussions with learners to assess their understanding of key elements involved in costing and pricing including factors such as material costs, labour, overhead, and market dynamics
Critique learners' write-ups on costing and pricing elements: Clarity and organisation, Accuracy and relevance

Engage learners in discussions to assess their integrity and ethical decision-making as they develop a costing and pricing checklist and accurately determine the cost of textile and clothing products while ensuring fairness and transparency in pricing
Observe learners' ability to apply mathematical skills in calculating unit production cost and selling price
Critique learners' costing and pricing checklists based on logical structure, accuracy and relevance
Engage learners in discussions to assess their understanding of the components of product marketing and selling
Observe learners' communication skills as they use a range of media to communicate ideas about the product
Engage learners in discussions to assess their proficiency in marketing textile and clothing products: Communication and presentation, Product branding, Customer engagement

Critique the effectiveness of learners' marketing approaches in the exhibition based on: Art of display, Product attractiveness, Pricing strategy, Environmental and health consideration, Customer care practices, Record-keeping practices, ICT integration

suggested_uses: Social media campaigns or influencing partnerships for advertising and promotions
Digital advertising and online marketing tools
ICT for product marketing and promotion

syllabus_notes.text_verbatim: Sub-topics: 9.1 Quality Control—Open Seams, Use of Correct Stitching Techniques, the Tension of the Thread Used in Stitching, Neatening of Raw Edges, Garment Fitting (36 periods); 9.2 Product Costing and Pricing (10 periods); 9.3 Product Marketing and Selling (26 periods)
